Write q_i=Q_i/k. Summing Q_i/sigma_i=Ha_i/2 gives H/2, hence the displayed chord normalization equals 2a_i/sqrt(q_i). Strict off-diagonal signs give |d_i|<s_i, and the column identities give sum s_i=1, so the open ball is necessary.

In the reverse direction g_i-|d_i| is at least epsilon by the triangle inequality. Subtracting s_i=|d_i|+epsilon/3 gives a_i at least epsilon/3 and each b_ij at least epsilon/6. Summing gives sum s_i=1 and sum a_i=1. With the two cyclic predecessor rows, the off-diagonal column sum is (s_{i+1}-d_{i+1}+s_{i+2}+d_{i+2})/2=a_i.

Each principal cofactor is positive because the product of the two off-diagonal column sums contains b_ij b_ji plus positive terms. Column balance bounds rank by two, so rank is exactly two. The identity adj(M)M=0 makes every adjugate row a multiple of the all-ones row; M adj(M)=0 then puts the common positive column in the right kernel. Normalizing gives positive barycentric coordinates. Any affine dependence of the first two column entries would have zero sum and lie in the same one-dimensional kernel, hence vanish. The third margin is minus the first two, so the specified spanning balanced normals give exactly M and the three strict incidences.

As an exact nonsymmetric spot check, d=(1/2,-1/4,0) yields 24M with rows (8,-13,-1), (-7,14,-1), (-1,-1,2). The principal cofactors of 24M are (27,15,21); the normalized kernel vector (9,5,7)/21 gives source zero. The prescribed squared row values are (21,35,1)/16.

The inverse d_i=u_i+u_{i+1}-1 works for every real u, and g_i-d_i=2(1-u_{i+1}). The all-plus/minus forms give the sum bounds and the three cyclic one-minus forms and their negatives give the six coordinate bounds. The identical argument holds with weak inequalities. The closed ball maps continuously because g_i>=|d_i|; its compact image is closed and every boundary image is the limit of images of contractions toward zero.
